title: What Makes Open Models Fast in Production — Sujee Maniyam, Nebius
talk_summary: A Nebius product talk on serving open models in production, covering their managed inference stack (inference, data lab, post-training, deployment) and serving optimizations like cache-aware routing, speculative decoding, KV cache offload, prefill/decode disaggregation, and quantization.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of load-balancing requests randomly across GPUs, they route requests to the node that already holds the matching KV cache prefix, keeping cache coherent and avoiding recomputation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the router knows where the caches are stored and it'll route them accordingly

takeaways.what_they_do: A small fast model drafts tokens and the large model verifies/regenerates, so most tokens come from the cheap model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: employ a smaller model which is a lot of the time faster and cheaper to generate the tokens but then have the large model verify
takeaways.numbers: up to 30% improvement with generic-trained draft models

takeaways.technique: Per-model engine fit / cheapest capable selection
takeaways.what_they_do: They benchmark which serving engine each model runs best on and deploy accordingly rather than assuming one engine fits all.
takeaways.evidence_quote: not all the models run equally well on all the engines. So we figure out which engines run well

takeaways.what_they_do: They experiment to find the quantization level that maximizes speed without degrading quality, rather than quantizing as aggressively as possible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do a lot of experiments to figure out like what's the kind of the sweet spot of a quantization

takeaways.technique: Production log capture into a data loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They import production completions into a data lab for filtering, versioning, and dataset export, then feed that back into post-training.
takeaways.evidence_quote: capture and structure the production logs ... slice and dice through these completions
